preparation, putting in order
fixed place, assigned position
H8498.detail:
1. The word primarily refers to the arrangement or general organization of a thing — the way its elements are arranged and ordered together. In Ezekiel 43:11, it refers to the "disposition" of the temple: how its rooms, entrances, and exits are arranged, how the space is structured.
2. This word can also mean the layout or physical structure of a building, construction, or object — somewhat like a plan or diagram that one might explain to someone to help them understand how things are assembled.
3. It can evoke the necessary preparation to put something in order, the action of preparing and organizing before building or executing a project.
4. The word can also designate a fixed place, a determined position where something or someone is established or assigned.
H8498.origine: This word comes from a root that expresses the idea of "fixing" or "establishing" — hence the image of a stable, organized, certainly established disposition. The Hebrew root evokes the action of giving a defined and lasting form to something. It is a term found in contexts of order and structure, related to the construction or organization of spaces.
H8498.emploi: The word appears only twice in the Hebrew Bible. In Ezekiel 43:11, God asks the prophet to make known to the Israelites the "disposition" of the temple — its forms, its entrances, its designs, so that they understand its structure and keep its ordinances. Thus, it is in a context of architectural and religious revelation. The context indicates that this word concerns the visible and understandable arrangement of a complex reality, here the divine sanctuary.
H8498.portee: This word invites the believer to recognize that God organizes all things according to a wise and intelligent order. The "disposition" of the temple revealed to Ezekiel shows that divine worship is not chaos, but a thoughtful structure, where each element has its place. For us, this suggests that faith requires a certain organization of life — clarity about our priorities, our commitments, the structure of our devotion to God.

sens: royal seat, place of power
the place where someone can be found or approached
the dwelling or seat of God
H8499.detail:
1. The word primarily refers to a seat, specifically the throne of a king — the furniture where the ruler sits. In Job 23:3, Job speaks of God's "throne" as the place where he might meet Him and present his case.
2. More broadly, it is a fixed place, an established position, a determined spot where one can find or stand before someone. This is why Job seeks to "come to His throne": he wants to know where God is so he can approach Him.
3. In the biblical context, the throne also represents the seat of divine power, the place from which God reigns and governs. It is a respectful term that acknowledges the authority and majesty of the one who occupies it.
H8499.origine: The word comes from a Hebrew root that means "to fix" or "to place" — the primary idea is that of a stable, established, fixed position. A throne is a fixed, permanent place. The word is a nominal form derived from the verb that expresses the action of putting in place or preparing something durably.
H8499.emploi: The word appears only once in the Hebrew Bible, in Job 23:3. Job is going through profound spiritual distress and cries out his desire to find God, to know where He sits so that he can appear before Him and present his case. The use of the word "throne" here is not descriptive (it is not about describing a piece of furniture or divine architecture), but existential: Job seeks the place, the seat, the fixed point where he can meet God. It is a call to the divine presence addressed to the one who occupies an eternal throne.
H8499.portee: This verse speaks to the heart of the believer who seeks God in the midst of suffering. Job expresses the fundamental desire of all prayer: to have access to God, to find the way to Him, to be heard by the one who reigns. The image of the divine throne reminds us that God is never absent or unreachable — He is seated on a stable and enduring throne. For the Christian, it is also an invitation to trust: the one who reigns from the throne of heaven can hear every prayer.
